slides.say: In the figure, each vertex of rectangle A B C D is the center of a circle with a radius of two centimeters. Point O is the center of a circle that is tangent to the four quarter circles, and to sides A D and B C. What is the area of rectangle A B C D, in square centimeters?
The area of a rectangle is length times width. The short side, A B, is four, and it's written in the figure. So we need the long side, A D.
Along A D, the first part is a radius of the quarter circle at A, so it's two. The last part is a radius of the quarter circle at D, so it's also two.
at: the first part is a radius

slides.say: But the part in the middle is hard. To calculate it, we need a helper line and Pythagoras. And if we don't see the helper line, we're stuck. So we'll solve it with an estimate.

slides: But wait. On the exam, a figure is not necessarily drawn to scale. So can I estimate from the figure?

slides.say: Usually, yes. First, most figures on the exam are drawn quite accurately. Second, a rule of thumb. With regular shapes, like a square, a circle, an equilateral triangle or a cube, the figure is accurate.

Why? Here, the circle in the middle touches the four quarter circles and two sides. There's only one way to draw that. If we make the figure bigger or smaller, all the parts keep the same ratios. So we can trust this figure. There's a whole lesson later about when a figure is accurate.
at: There's only one way to draw

slides.say: [pause] So let's compare the middle part with lengths we know. Here it is again, under the rectangle.
It's longer than a radius, which is two. And it's shorter than the diameter of the circle in the middle, which is four.

slides: If it's hard to see, use your eraser on the exam. Mark the length of a radius on it, and compare.

slides.say: So the middle part is between two and four.
at: So the middle part is between

slides.say: The whole side A D is made of two, plus the middle, plus two. Two plus two plus two is six, and two plus four plus two is eight. So A D is between six and eight.
The area is four times A D. Four times six is twenty-four, and four times eight is thirty-two. So the area is between twenty-four and thirty-two, and it isn't equal to either one.
[pause] Now the choices. Choice number four, forty, is more than thirty-two. It's out.
Choice number three, thirty-two. The middle part is less than four, so the area is less than thirty-two. It's out too.

Choice number two, sixteen root two. The area has to be more than twenty-four. Sixteen times one and a half is sixteen plus eight, twenty-four. So to pass twenty-four, the root has to be more than one and a half.
at: Sixteen times one and a half

slides.say: But one and a half squared is two and a quarter, which is more than two. So root two is less than one and a half, and sixteen root two is less than twenty-four. It's out.
at: But one and a half squared
sixteen root two is less than twenty-four

slides.say: Three choices are out, so choice number one, sixteen root three, is our answer.
